AGENDA
  YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMITTEE
  Tuesday, October 26, 2021
  6:30 P.M.
  The three-fold mission of the Youth & Family Action Committee is:
  1. To support positive activities and opportunities for young people;
  2. To strengthen families; and
  3. To combat the problems of substance abuse.

Tonight’s meeting will be held virtually in compliance with Governor Newson’s Executive
Order to minimize the spread of the COVID-19 Virus. The meeting will be live streamed on
the La Verne You Tube channel at www.cityoflaverne.org/stream.

To make a comment on an agenda item or under public comment, email your phone
number to cityclerk@cityoflaverne.org. This email address will be monitored live during the
meeting and interested parties will be called. Please be aware there is a delay in the live
stream service and any requests to speak should be submitted as soon as possible.

minutes_text:
LA VERNE YOUTH & FAMILY ACTION COMMIfiEE
  Minutes of the Regular Meeting
  October 26,2021

1. A regular meeting of the Youth & Family Action Committee was called to order by
  Chair Robin Carder at 6:30 p.m.

2. Executive Board Members present (virtually):
  Executive Board
  Robin Carder, Chair - Council Member
  Rick Crosby, Vice Chair - Council Member
  Greg Palatto - BUSD
  Denise Fisher - Resident

  Don Kendrick, Resident
  Ron Serven, Resident
  Mark Rodgers, BUSD
  Sam Gonzalez, LVPD
  Hollie Savage, LVPD
  Chris Dransfeldt, LVPD
  Janessa Gonzalez, LVPD
  Bree Baumgartner, Bonita H.S.
  Jubilee Nyd, Bonita H.S.
  Michelle Robinson, Tri-City Mental Health
  JR Ranells, City of La Veme
  Alfie Sanchez, Majestic Cycling/Kiwanis lntemational
  Kathy Sanchez, Majestic Cycling

3. Review of Minutes  Minutes for the September 28,2021 , meeting were
  approved.

4. School Resource Officer  School Resource Officer Janessa Gonzalez provided
  a report to the group noting that things were back in
  full swing and keeping her busy. Janessa introduced
  the new student representative Jubilee Nyd who is a
  senior at Bonita High School. Jubilee is interested in
  pursulng a career in law enforcement and Janessa
  will mentor him this school year.

  The group also discussed the potential impacts of the
  tobacco ordinance and that the effective date is
  January 1 .

5. Bike Give Away Event  JR Ranells with the City reviewed progress on putting
  together the bike give away event and has engaged
  the Community Services Department for help. The
  event is tentatively scheduled for Saturday, December
  4th and will take place prior to the Holiday Stroll event
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 26, 202'1, page 2

  in old town. Alfie Sanchez with Majestic Cycling and
  the Kiwanis also provided information on the remaining
  efforts to build the bikes and coordinate storing them.

6. Budget Update  JR provided information on the budget. Due to
  COVID, YFAC has not had any expenditures since
  November 2020 and still has a remaining balance of
  $17,520.83. The group reviewed the last report and
  received information on the continuation of treasurer
  duties from David & MargareULeRoy Haynes. Since
  an annual budget was not adopted, any expenditures
  will be brought before the Executive Board for
  approval.

  The group also discussed the need to begin thinking
  about possible fundraising activities as once regular
  program support resumes, the remaining funds will
  quickly be exhausted.

7. Tri-City School Counseling  Michelle Robinson with Tri-City Mental Health provided
  an introduction of herself and her history with Tri-City.
  Michelle also detailed the school counseling program
  in partnership with BUSD and noted that not as many
  school sites would be participating due largely to lack
  of adequate meeting space as a result of COVID
  adjustments. While the Tri-City program may be
  reduced compared to previous years, BUSD has
  implemented more on site and expanded mental
  health services for students. JR shared that YFAC
  has traditionally funded up to $6,000 annually for the
  Tri-City program and BUSD has requested the same
  level of support for this school year. However, since
  the program will be at less locations there may be less
  cost depending on if hours of service increase or
  remain as in previous years. The Executive Board
  formally voted to approve an amount not to exceed
  $6,000 in support of the program.

8. Executive Board Vacancies  Chair Robin Carder informed the group that long and
  dedicated serving Executive Board Member Carolyn
  Cockrell submitted her resignation creating a vacancy
  for a resident position. An application period has
  opened for those interested in serving the community
  on YFAC and the City Council will ultimately appoint
  someone to fill the vacancy. Chair Carder shared that
  Don Kendrick has previously served on the Executive
  Board when he was on the City Council and is a long
  time participant of YFAC going back to its early
 Youth & Family Action Committee Minutes October 26, 2021, page 3

  inception making him a strong candidate. Vice Chair
  Crosby noted that it would be prudent to review all
  applications prior to making a recommendation to the
  City Council.

  Don agreed that reviewing all applications would be
  wise of the Executive Board and shared that he was
  interested in serving. Don noted his longstanding
  involvement with YFAC and shared many highlights of
  programs he helped to grow for the benefit of the
  community.

  The group noted that if others in attendance were
  considering submitting an application they were
  welcome to share their thoughts on serving. After no
  additional discussion, the Executive Board encouraged
  people to apply with the City Clerk's office. Staff was
  directed to bring back all submitted applications to a
  November meeting for the Committee to review and
  make a recommendation for appointment to the City
  Council.

9. Public Comment  Administrative Lieutenant Sam Gonzalez informed the
  group of his pending promotion to Police Captain and
  introduced Lieutenant Chris Dransfeldt who will be
  representing the department at future YFAC meetings.

  Alfie Sanchez noted that there are some future
  opportunities to sponsor/fundraise for YFAC through
  cycling and similar special events.

  Based on the upcoming holidays, the group suggested
  that a special November meeting be held on Tuesday,
  November 16, 2021 , and that the regular November
  and December meetings be canceled.

10. Next Meeting  The next YFAC meeting is scheduled for November
  'l6th at 6:30 p.m.

1  1. Adjournment  The meeting was adjourned at 7:30 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

JR Ranells
Assistant to the City Manager
